title: A village built around a university
lede: In the early 1920s the Janss family set out to develop the old Wolfskill ranch west of Beverly Hills with a plan: help bring the University of California to its hills, then sell everyone else the homes and shops around it. UCLA moved in in 1929, Westwood Village opened the same year, and its Spanish-style streets and movie palaces became the Westside's downtown.

p: The Janss brothers took over thousands of acres of ranch land between Beverly Hills and Sawtelle and made the University of California the centerpiece of their plan. With a campus on the hill, they reasoned, the houses and shops around it would sell themselves. Voters approved bonds to buy the campus land in 1925, and the Janss company laid out Westwood Village below it, with Mediterranean architecture, tile roofs and design rules for every building.

fact: the first class taught in Westwood
p: UCLA began on Vermont Avenue in East Hollywood in 1919 and outgrew it within a decade. On May 31, 1929, classes on Vermont were dismissed early and a police motorcade led trucks of furniture to the new campus, where Royce Hall and the library stood almost alone on the hill. The first class held in Westwood was Chemistry 1A.

Westwood Village opened alongside the university and quickly became the Westside's shopping district. The Fox Village Theatre, with its white tower, opened in 1931, and the Bruin followed in 1937. The two theaters still host Hollywood premieres, and the Village remains one of the few walkable, master-planned business districts of its era in Los Angeles.
